title: Accounts Memorandum — Counting the Days Charged for Re-Synchronising a Controls Database
content:
# Accounts Memorandum — Counting the Days Charged for Re-Synchronising a Controls Database

**The count.** Where the tier's help desk answers around the clock and the plan under the Building Automation Service Plans carries a day on which monitoring was last restored, the days charged for re-synchronisation are counted from that day to the handling day. Where the tier's help desk answers extended hours or business hours only and the twelve months to the handling day carry three or more charges that fell due on the plan, the days charged for re-synchronisation are counted from the due day of the plan's most recent plan fee charge to the handling day, that due day excluded and the handling day included. In every other case the days charged for re-synchronisation are counted from the day monitoring was withdrawn to the handling day, that day excluded and the handling day included.

| Hours the tier's help desk answers | Other condition | The days are counted from |
|---|---|---|
| around the clock | the plan carries a day on which monitoring was last restored | that day, to the handling day |
| around the clock | the plan carries no such day | the day monitoring was withdrawn, to the handling day |
| extended hours or business hours only | 3 or more charges fell due on the plan in the twelve months to the handling day | the due day of the plan's most recent plan fee charge, to the handling day |
| extended hours or business hours only | fewer than 3 such charges | the day monitoring was withdrawn, to the handling day |

## Points of judgement

- The count in the third row is of charges that fell due in the twelve months to the handling day; exactly 3 such charges meets it.
- Where the days are counted from the due day of the most recent plan fee charge, that due day is excluded and the handling day included; where they are counted from the day monitoring was withdrawn, that day is excluded and the handling day included.

## Worked case (hypothetical)

A plan at a tier answering extended hours, whose monitoring was withdrawn 100 days before the handling day, whose most recent plan fee charge fell due 55 days before the handling day, and which carries 4 charges fallen due in the twelve months, has 55 days charged for re-synchronisation. Had only 2 charges fallen due in that window, the days charged would be the 100 days since monitoring was withdrawn.
